title: Discharging the Unit-Circle Converse Axiom of Ptolemy's Theorem (Positive Proportionality ⇒ Cyclic Order)
description: Proves, 0-axiom, the angular step the unit-circle converse leaf ptolemys-theorem-oq-01-oq-01 had to assume as axiom positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order: for four distinct points on the unit circle, positive real proportionality of the opposite-side products t·(z₁-z₂)(z₃-z₄) = (z₂-z₃)(z₁-z₄) with t > 0 forces a counterclockwise or clockwise cyclic order. The headline positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order_thm has exactly the parent axiom's statement, now a theorem; ptolemy_equality_implies_ccw_or_cw_axiomfree then reproduces the parent's converse (Ptolemy equality ⇒ CCW or CW) without that axiom. The proof anchors at z₁ = exp(iθ₁) and writes every other point as zⱼ = z₁·exp(iφⱼ) with φⱼ ∈ (0, 2π) (angle extraction via Complex.arg and a 2π shift), so zⱼ = exp(i(θ₁+φⱼ)). The half-angle factorisation exp(iα) - exp(iβ) = 2i·sin((α-β)/2)·exp(i(α+β)/2) collapses the complex proportionality to the real equation t·sin((θ₁-θ₂)/2)·sin((θ₃-θ₄)/2) = sin((θ₂-θ₃)/2)·sin((θ₁-θ₄)/2): the four exponential phase factors all combine to exp(i(θ₁+θ₂+θ₃+θ₄)/2) and cancel, as do the two (2i)² factors. Substituting θⱼ = θ₁+φⱼ makes sin((θ₁-θ₂)/2) = -sin(φ₂/2) and sin((θ₁-θ₄)/2) = -sin(φ₄/2) negative, so with t > 0 the remaining two half-angle sines share a sign, which by monotonicity of sin on (-π,π) means φ₃ lies strictly between φ₂ and φ₄ — i.e. φ₂ < φ₃ < φ₄ (CCW) or φ₄ < φ₃ < φ₂ (CW). #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

overview.historicalContext: Ptolemy's theorem and its converse — equality in Ptolemy's inequality holds exactly when the four points are concyclic in cyclic order — date to the Almagest. Mathlib formalises Ptolemy's inequality (EuclideanGeometry.mul_dist_le_mul_dist_add_mul_dist) and the strict-convexity equality case behind it, but its source explicitly lacks a 'cyclic polygon' concept, so the converse for points on a circle is not available off the shelf. The gallery's unit-circle leaf ptolemys-theorem-oq-01-oq-01 proves that converse for four points on the unit circle but seals its single trigonometric step behind axiom positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order: that positive real proportionality of the opposite-side products forces counterclockwise or clockwise order. The axiom's own docstring promised the proof would be 'a finite sign analysis of the three interlacing patterns of four angles.' This entry delivers exactly that, discharging the axiom so the unit-circle converse becomes 0-axiom.
overview.problemStatement: Prove (not assume) that for four distinct unit-circle points z₁,z₂,z₃,z₄, the existence of t > 0 with t·(z₁-z₂)(z₃-z₄) = (z₂-z₃)(z₁-z₄) implies IsCCWOrder z₁ z₂ z₃ z₄ ∨ IsCWOrder z₁ z₂ z₃ z₄, and hence that Ptolemy equality alone (via the strict-convexity proportionality extraction) implies cyclic order — both 0-axiom / 0-sorry.
overview.text: Fix θ₁ with z₁ = exp(iθ₁) (Complex.norm_mul_exp_arg_mul_I, ‖z₁‖ = 1). For each other point z, the ratio z/z₁ has modulus 1 and is ≠ 1, so it equals exp(iφ) for a unique φ ∈ (0,2π) (take arg of the ratio, shift by 2π when negative); hence zⱼ = z₁·exp(iφⱼ) = exp(i(θ₁+φⱼ)). The half-angle identity exp(iα) - exp(iβ) = 2i·sin((α-β)/2)·exp(i(α+β)/2) factors each of the four differences; both opposite-side products become (-4)·(product of two half-angle sines)·exp(i(θ₁+θ₂+θ₃+θ₄)/2), the phase factor and the -4 being common. Cancelling the common nonzero factor turns the complex proportionality into the real identity t·sin((θ₁-θ₂)/2)·sin((θ₃-θ₄)/2) = sin((θ₂-θ₃)/2)·sin((θ₁-θ₄)/2). With θⱼ = θ₁+φⱼ the arguments (θ₁-θ₂)/2 = -φ₂/2 and (θ₁-θ₄)/2 = -φ₄/2 lie in (-π,0), so sin there is negative; t > 0 then forces sin((φ₃-φ₄)/2) and sin((φ₂-φ₃)/2) to have the same sign. Since these arguments lie in (-π,π), where sin(x/2) > 0 ⇔ x > 0, the common sign says φ₃ is strictly between φ₂ and φ₄: φ₂ < φ₃ < φ₄ gives the CCW witnesses (θ₁, θ₁+φ₂, θ₁+φ₃, θ₁+φ₄), while φ₄ < φ₃ < φ₂ gives the CW witnesses (= CCW order of z₁,z₄,z₃,z₂).
overview.proofStrategy: ANGLE EXTRACTION (unit_to_angle, ratio_angle): a unit number ≠ 1 is exp(iφ) for φ ∈ (0,2π) via Complex.norm_mul_exp_arg_mul_I, the arg bounds neg_pi_lt_arg / arg_le_pi, and Complex.exp_two_pi_mul_I for the 2π shift; ratio_angle applies this to z/z₁ (modulus 1, ≠ 1 since z ≠ z₁). REDUCTION (reduce_to_sines): rewrite all four differences with the locally re-derived exp_diff_factor, factor both products into scalar·(-4)·(E₂₃·E₁₄) using the phase identity E₁₂·E₃₄ = E₂₃·E₁₄ (exp_add + ring) and Complex.I_sq, cancel the common nonzero (-4)·(E₂₃·E₁₄) with mul_right_cancel₀, then descend to ℝ by exact_mod_cast. SIGN ANALYSIS (positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order_thm): set A = sin(φ₂/2) > 0, D = sin(φ₄/2) > 0 (sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi); fold the two leading negatives so the equation reads t·A·C = B·D with B = sin((φ₂-φ₃)/2), C = sin((φ₃-φ₄)/2); a trichotomy on C transfers its sign to B (t,A,D > 0), and the helpers half_sin_pos_iff / half_sin_neg_iff translate the signs into φ₃ < φ₄ ∧ φ₂ < φ₃ (CCW) or φ₄ < φ₃ ∧ φ₃ < φ₂ (CW), supplying the IsCCWOrder / IsCWOrder angle witnesses directly. CORROLLARY (ptolemy_equality_implies_ccw_or_cw_axiomfree): feed Ptolemy equality through the local ptolemy_eq_implies_pos_prop (the strict-convexity proportionality extraction ptolemy_equality_implies_proportional) into the discharged theorem.
keyInsights: **The axiom is just a sign computation once the angles are pinned down.** Anchoring at z₁ and writing every other point as z₁·exp(iφⱼ) with φⱼ ∈ (0,2π) turns 'cyclic order' into 'φ₃ between φ₂ and φ₄', and the proportionality hypothesis into a single real sine equation whose sign content selects exactly that betweenness.

**Two of the four half-angle sines have a forced sign.** Because (θ₁-θ₂)/2 = -φ₂/2 and (θ₁-θ₄)/2 = -φ₄/2 lie in (-π,0), sin((θ₁-θ₂)/2) and sin((θ₁-θ₄)/2) are negative for free; t > 0 then propagates a single sign condition to the remaining pair, and that is all that distinguishes CCW/CW from the excluded interlaced orderings.

**The exponential phases cancel exactly.** Both opposite-side products carry the same total phase exp(i(θ₁+θ₂+θ₃+θ₄)/2) and the same (2i)² = -4, so the complex proportionality is equivalent to a purely real identity in the half-angle sines — no appeal to the modulus of either product is needed.

**Discharging beats the inversion route for the angular facet.** The sibling circle→line entry (oq-03-oq-01) and the parent equality-case entry (oq-03) handle the unordered/coordinate-free facets via inversion; the ORDERED unit-circle facet is most directly settled by this finite trigonometric sign analysis, exactly as the axiom's docstring anticipated.
prerequisites: Polar form of a unit complex number: Complex.norm_mul_exp_arg_mul_I, with arg bounds Complex.neg_pi_lt_arg and Complex.arg_le_pi, and 2π-periodicity via Complex.exp_two_pi_mul_I
The half-angle difference identity exp(iα) - exp(iβ) = 2i·sin((α-β)/2)·exp(i(α+β)/2) (re-derived locally as exp_diff_factor from exp_ofReal_mul_I_re/_im and product-to-sum)
Sign of sine on a half-period: Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi and Real.sin_neg, packaged as half_sin_pos_iff / half_sin_neg_iff on (-2π,2π)
The strict-convexity proportionality extraction ptolemy_equality_implies_proportional (Ptolemy equality ⇒ positive proportionality) from PtolemysComplexProofOQ01
The parent definition IsCCWOrder (existence of strictly increasing angles within one period) from PtolemysTheoremOQ01

sections.title: Header: discharging the cyclic-order axiom via half-angle sines
sections.summary: States what this file proves — the parent leaf's axiom `positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order` (positive real proportionality of the opposite-side products forces a CCW/CW order on the unit circle) is discharged as a theorem — and sketches the proof: anchoring at z_1, converting the complex proportionality into a real sine equation via a half-angle factorization, then reading the order off the sign and monotonicity of sin.
sections.mathContext: $t\cdot\sin(\tfrac{\theta_1-\theta_2}2)\sin(\tfrac{\theta_3-\theta_4}2)=\sin(\tfrac{\theta_2-\theta_3}2)\sin(\tfrac{\theta_1-\theta_4}2)$ with $t>0$ forces $\varphi_3$ between $\varphi_2,\varphi_4$, giving CCW or CW order.

The parent leaf PtolemysTheoremOQ01OQ01 — which declares the axiom and these definitions — currently fails to elaborate under Mathlib v4.26.0 because of unrelated API drift (Complex.abs_apply, Real.sqrt_eq_iff_sq_eq removed) in a numerical sanity-example, so this file restates the small definitions to stay independent of that breakage while discharging an identical statement.

sections.mathContext: The two engines of the proof: turning complex differences into sines, and reading off the sign of a half-angle sine.

sections.title: Reducing the Complex Proportionality to a Real Sine Equation
sections.summary: reduce_to_sines: substituting the four factorisations, both opposite-side products become scalar·(-4)·(E₂₃·E₁₄) via the phase identity E₁₂·E₃₄ = E₂₃·E₁₄ and Complex.I_sq; cancelling the common nonzero factor and casting down to ℝ yields t·sin((θ₁-θ₂)/2)·sin((θ₃-θ₄)/2) = sin((θ₂-θ₃)/2)·sin((θ₁-θ₄)/2).
sections.mathContext: The complex hypothesis is equivalent to a single real identity in the half-angle sines — the bridge from algebra to the sign analysis.

sections.title: Angle Extraction
sections.summary: unit_to_angle: a unit complex number ≠ 1 equals exp(iφ) for a unique φ ∈ (0,2π). ratio_angle: anchored form — a unit point z ≠ z₁ is z₁·exp(iφ) with φ ∈ (0,2π), obtained by applying unit_to_angle to z/z₁.
sections.mathContext: Pins every point to an angle in one period above the anchor θ₁, so 'cyclic order' becomes an ordering of the φⱼ.

sections.title: The Discharged Axiom and the Axiom-Free Converse
sections.summary: positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order_thm: the parent axiom, proved — positive proportionality forces CCW or CW order via the sign analysis. ptolemy_equality_implies_ccw_or_cw_axiomfree: the parent's converse (Ptolemy equality ⇒ CCW or CW), now reproduced without the positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order axiom.
sections.mathContext: The payload: the unit-circle converse of Ptolemy's theorem, axiom-free.

conclusion.summary: A machine-checked Lean 4 proof that, for four distinct unit-circle points, positive real proportionality of the opposite-side products forces counterclockwise or clockwise cyclic order — exactly the statement the unit-circle converse leaf assumed as axiom positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order. Anchoring at z₁ = exp(iθ₁) and writing the others as exp(i(θ₁+φⱼ)) with φⱼ ∈ (0,2π), the half-angle factorisation reduces the complex proportionality to t·sin((θ₁-θ₂)/2)·sin((θ₃-θ₄)/2) = sin((θ₂-θ₃)/2)·sin((θ₁-θ₄)/2); two forced-negative sines plus t > 0 leave a single sign condition that places φ₃ strictly between φ₂ and φ₄, i.e. CCW or CW order. The file is 0-axiom, 0-sorry (#print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only), and the corollary ptolemy_equality_implies_ccw_or_cw_axiomfree reproduces the parent's converse without the axiom.
conclusion.implications: Removes the last assumption from the unit-circle converse of Ptolemy's theorem in the gallery: the chain Ptolemy equality ⇒ positive proportionality ⇒ cyclic order is now end-to-end machine-checked with no trigonometric ordering axiom. Together with the parent equality-case entry (inversion/betweenness, oq-03) and the sibling circle→line duality (oq-03-oq-01), the unordered and ordered facets of 'Ptolemy equality ⇔ concyclic in cyclic order' are all 0-axiom. The proof is exactly the finite sign analysis the axiom's docstring promised.
openQuestions: Promote the disjunction IsCCWOrder ∨ IsCWOrder to a single oriented statement using Mathlib's oriented angle Complex.arg / Real.Angle, eliminating the CW relabelling and exposing a canonical winding.

Transport the unit-circle discharge to the general circle (arbitrary centre/radius) by normalising through (z - c)/r, matching the concyclic wrapper ptolemy_equality_for_concyclic and yielding an axiom-free 'Ptolemy equality ⇔ concyclic-in-cyclic-order' for arbitrary circles.

crossReferences.description: Parent unit-circle converse leaf. It proves Ptolemy equality ⇔ CCW/CW order but assumes axiom positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order for the angular step. This entry discharges that axiom (positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order_thm has the identical statement) and reproduces the converse axiom-free (ptolemy_equality_implies_ccw_or_cw_axiomfree).

Grandparent equality-case entry: characterises Ptolemy equality by Wbtw of inversion images in any Euclidean space (the coordinate-free, ordered facet). This entry settles the unit-circle ordered facet directly via the half-angle sign analysis.
Sibling circle→line duality: proves Cospherical ⇔ inversion images on a hyperplane (the unordered facet), axiom-free. Complementary to this entry's ordered, cyclic-order facet.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None beyond the explicit hypotheses (four distinct points on the unit circle, ‖zⱼ‖ = 1, and positive proportionality t > 0 with t·(z₁-z₂)(z₃-z₄) = (z₂-z₃)(z₁-z₄)). Verified 0 axioms, 0 sorries: #print axioms on positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order_thm and ptolemy_equality_implies_ccw_or_cw_axiomfree reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] — no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool, and crucially no positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order. IsCCWOrder is imported from PtolemysTheoremOQ01; IsCWOrder/FourDistinct are restated verbatim because the parent leaf PtolemysTheoremOQ01OQ01 (which declares the axiom) currently has unrelated Mathlib-v4.26.0 drift in a numerical sanity-example.
originalContributions: positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order_thm: the parent's axiom positive_ratio_implies_cyclic_order, proved as a theorem — for four distinct unit-circle points, positive real proportionality of the opposite-side products implies IsCCWOrder ∨ IsCWOrder, via angle extraction and a finite half-angle sign analysis.
ptolemy_equality_implies_ccw_or_cw_axiomfree: the parent's converse (Ptolemy equality ⇒ counterclockwise or clockwise order), reproduced with no trigonometric ordering axiom.

reduce_to_sines: a reusable reduction collapsing the complex proportionality t·(z₁-z₂)(z₃-z₄) = (z₂-z₃)(z₁-z₄) (with zⱼ = exp(iθⱼ)) to the real identity t·sin((θ₁-θ₂)/2)·sin((θ₃-θ₄)/2) = sin((θ₂-θ₃)/2)·sin((θ₁-θ₄)/2) by cancelling the common phase and (2i)² factors.
unit_to_angle / ratio_angle: angle extraction placing each unit point at a unique φ ∈ (0,2π) above the anchor θ₁, the device that turns cyclic order into an ordering of the φⱼ.
half_sin_pos_iff / half_sin_neg_iff: sign of sin(x/2) on (-2π,2π) characterised by the sign of x, the bridge from the real sine identity to the φ-betweenness.
mathlibDependencies: Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi, Real.sin_neg, Real.cos_add, Real.cos_sub, Real.sin_add, Real.sin_sub
